text:
Recent research supports separating sampled-ranking diagnostics from catalog behavior. [Subbiah et al. (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06371) show that correcting negative-sampling rank estimates improves WARP/LambdaRank training; this does not establish that larger sampled-negative margins imply better full-catalog recommendations. [Distributionally-Informed Recommender System Evaluation (2024)](https://841.io/doc/disteval.html) argues for examining user-level distributions and uncertainty beyond aggregate scores. [Scalable Data Debugging (RecSys 2025)](https://deem.berlin/publication/2025-07-03-scalable-data-debugging-for-neighborhood-based-recommendation-with-data-shapley-values-recsys/) provides an actionable debugging example through identifying influential interactions, although its neighborhood models differ from SASRec.

No directly matching study surfaced validating diagnostic probes through controlled faults and matched backbone/recent-residual comparisons. Suggested experiment, rather than established finding: inject reversible faults separately—shuffle sequence order, suppress recent history, perturb item embeddings, amplify popularity scores—and test whether probes detect their intended failure with increasing severity. Compare backbone-only and residual variants using identical users, candidates, seeds, and training budgets. Bootstrap paired per-user HR@10 differences within each category, then recompute the four-category macro-average; these intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fixed candidates and trained models. Keep full-catalog unseen-item coverage, popularity concentration, and recommendation overlap as separate behavioral diagnostics for the 20 simulator users. Treat a probe as actionable only when its predicted intervention improves pinned validation HR@10 across matched comparisons. Repeated adaptive selection needs caution: [Rink and Brannath (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10994-024-06632-w) address post-selection uncertainty, which ordinary bootstrap intervals do not automatically resolve.
